title: Rams starting LB exits vs. 49ers with hip injury
description: Rams LB Omar Speights exited in the first half with a hip injury and was replaced by Shaun Dolac.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams came into Week 1 remarkably healthy, but one of their defensive starters suffered an injury in the first half of the opener against the San Francisco 49ers. Linebacker Omar Speights exited in the first half with a hip injury and the Rams are calling him questionable to return.

Second-year linebacker Shaun Dolac replaced Speights on defense next to Nate Landman. Speights started 16 games for the Rams last season and entered this year as a starter alongside Landman.

Update: Speights has returned to the game, taking the field again in the second quarter.

title: Toronto Blue Jays Alejandro Kirk Has Personal News Emerge Before Orioles Series
description: Toronto Blue Jays catcher Alejandro Kirk has personal news emerge before their series against the Baltimore Orioles. The post Toronto Blue Jays Alejandro Kirk Has Personal News Emerge Before Orioles Series appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Toronto Blue Jays wouldn't be where they are without the talents of Alejandro Kirk. While the team is obviously disappointed by the results from Wednesday night's game against the Oakland Athletics, they have all the right pieces to make a true run for the MLB playoffs.

Before their first game against the Baltimore Orioles, Kirk shared some personal news.

Before the first pitch of their new series against the Orioles, Kirk took to Instagram to share some personal news.

In an Instagram story, he shared a Team Mexico baseball card fans can buy. In the caption, he wrote, "Collect my card."

Bowman Chrome created the card he revealed in his story.

Kirk is a 27-year-old catcher who has played 68 games this season. In those games, Kirk has recorded 66 hits, 36 RBIs, seven doubles, and nine home runs.

Kirk has spent seven seasons with the Blue Jays organization.

He has been the everyday catcher for the Blue Jays for several years. Before this year, he didn't play less than 100 games for four consecutive years.

As far as his future is concerned, Kirk is in the first year of a five-year $58 million extension.

However, with the emergence of Brandon Valenzuela, his future as the everyday starter could be called into question. But that decision will depend on what George Springer's future with the organization is.

There are two ways forward. Either Valenzuela and Kirk split time at catcher, or Kirk can play as the DH. This plan hinges on Springer moving on from the Blue Jays in the offseason.

Despite his injuries, Kirk has been on a hot streak recently. He and Kazuma Okamoto have been providing consistent offense for a team desperately lacking power.

Whichever way things go this offseason, the Blue Jays will be covered at catcher. If Kirk is not being the plate, they are in good hands with Valenzuela.

title: Penn State Starter Has Perfect Response After Below-Average First Game
description: It was a very impressive Week 1 for Penn State against Marshall. Taking care of business and shutting out a Marshall team that's above average is always a step in the right direction.
fullText:
It was a very impressive Week 1 for Penn State against Marshall. Taking care of business and shutting out a Marshall team that's above average is always a step in the right direction.

However, as we dissect what Penn State did, it's only fair to point out some of the problems it had on both sides of the football.

Defensively speaking, I was very impressed with what the Nittany Lions did, and putting up a shutout only confirmed that.

Head coach Matt Campbell is going to be a defensive-minded type of guy, and with Penn State historically being one of the better defensive teams in the country year in and year out, he fits that mold perfectly.

Penn State has done a lot of things well over the past few decades, but running the football at a high level is nearly constant. There's a reason why Penn State is typically one of the better running teams in college football, and that can't change. In the Big Ten, Penn State needs to run the football at a high level to be the team it aspires to be.

Regarding how Penn State looked on the run side of things in its first game against Marshall, I don't think it's unfair to say it was very disappointing. If the Nittany Lions want to win games at a high level in the Big Ten, there's no debate that they need to run the football at a much higher clip.

That's something that players and coaches have spoken about, including running back Carson Hansen, who understands that how he looked the other day was inexcusable.

"I think we had a lot more," Hansen told reporters Wednesday in the Lasch Building, per StateCollege.com. "I think we got to refine our little details. We got to find those little things that are gonna make this offense explode, and that's exciting because we have the potential to do that, and I'm excited for this next Saturday."

"As a running back, you want as much as you can, because you're a competitive guy, and whatever they bring at you, you gotta be prepared for it, and that's the mindset going into it," Hansen said. "If they pack the box, that is what it is, and we got to go run through it. If not, we'll throw it over top, and you know we'll get it done that way."

I'm glad that Hansen isn't trying to beat around the bush here and say that Penn State did what it had to do on that end of things.

Instead of coming out and making excuses about how poor it looked, Hansen knows that for Penn State to do what's needed, it has to improve in that area. I expect that to be the case pretty soon, as there's just far too much talent on that front for it to continue.

title: Temple Coach Has High Praise for Penn State Prior to Week 2 Game
description: Penn State has a very interesting game coming up on Saturday against Temple. As the Nittany Lions look to go 2-0 to start their season, there's really not much of a reason why they shouldn't win this game, to say the least.
fullText:
Penn State has a very interesting game coming up on Saturday against Temple. As the Nittany Lions look to go 2-0 to start their season, there's really not much of a reason why they shouldn't win this game, to say the least.

The line is a bit strange at just about 23.5, but regardless, Penn State is in a very good spot to go 2-0.

There are also some other ways to look at this game for Penn State. While playing at Lincoln Financial Field doesn't necessarily make this a road game for the Nittany Lions because of the number of Penn State fans that should be at that game, it'll be a good test to play away from Beaver Stadium.

Temple also recognizes the opportunity.

Not that Temple is going to be some Group of Five team that has a chance to make the College Football Playoff, but beating Penn State or at least competing with the Nittany Lions would be a very good sign for its program. Speaking to reporters, that's something that the Temple coaching staff understands is a reality.

"I watch Penn State, I am really impressed with their defense. They are long. They're athletic. They have a lot of them — they got five defensive ends that are all like really good football players. So I was really, really impressed with their defense."

"I know Coach Campbell's in the infancy of putting together what he envisions up there. I think he was a phenomenal choice to be the head coach there. I know him a little bit, and we did some things together, some clinics together. I spent a little time with him, and I heard him speak. I think he was a home run in terms of, you know, what he can do with that program and how they can build it," K.C. Keeler said, per Centre Daily.

Defensively speaking, as Keeler touched on here, Penn State is going to come out and do what's needed on both sides of the football. As we've seen over the past few years, the Nittany Lions typically have one of the best defenses in college football, and that's not going to change with Matt Campbell as the head coach.

title: Our experts predict Cincinnati Bengals season. Check it out
description: The Bengals had a big offseason. Did they do enough to return to the playoffs? Check out the Cincinnati.com staff' Bengals season predictions.
fullText:
Ahead of the Cincinnati Bengals' season opener against Tampa Bay on Sept. 13, Cincinnati.com Bengals beat reporter Kelsey Conway, columnist Jason Williams, reporter Pat Brennan and sports editor Jason Hoffman make their annual season predictions. Here is their final record and game-by-game predictions:

Conway: After a disastrous 2025 season, the Bengals have completely changed the vibes around the team. They just enjoyed one of the most productive, low drama training camps the franchise has seen in years. They will be ready to play in front of their home fans and deliver a win to start the season strong. Pick: Bengals 27, Buccaneers 20

Williams: Tampa Bay hasn't lost a season opener since 2020, and coach Todd Bowles does a fantastic job developing pass-rush game plans. The Bucs are one of those competitive teams that can beat anyone, and it all doesn't bode well for the traditionally slow-starting Bengals. Pick: Buccaneers 24, Bengals 21

Brennan: Now in the last year of his contract, Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield seems to have a bigger chip on his shoulder than usual, and something to prove. That's a scary proposition for a revamped but yet-to-be-truly-tested Cincinnati defense because Mayfield has the ingredients to not only make it a long day at Paycor Stadium, but he could actually will Tampa to a win. Cincinnati will hang on for the victory, but get ready for a tight one. Pick: Bengals 31, Buccaneers 30.

Conway: Houston's defense was the NFL's best in 2025, and they return majority of the group. With this game being on the road, I expect the Bengals' offense to struggle a bit, and ultimately not be able to score enough points to win the game. Pick: Texans 21, Bengals 10

Williams: Not an ideal Game 2 for the Bengals – on the road against a team that's gone to the playoffs three straight seasons and is expected to contend for the postseason again. Pick: Texans 23, Bengals 20

Brennan: It's the home opener for a Texans team that expects to contend and has solid quarterback play. All those ingredients make this too tall of an order for the Bengals in the Week 2 stage of their development. Pick: Texans 28, Bengals 17.

Conway: The Bengals understand that if they want to contend for the AFC North title, they must sweep the Steelers. If Cincinnati's offensive line can hold up against Pittsburgh's defensive front, the Bengals can exploit what I expect to be a weak Pittsburgh secondary. Pick: Bengals 34, Steelers 21

Williams: The Bengals offense gets settled in, and this is where Cincinnati puts it all together. Expect the Bengals' stars to shine in this rivalry game, as Joe Burrow and Dexter Lawrence will have a big day. Pick: Bengals 28, Steelers 17

Brennan: The Bengals have to handle their business in the AFC North − period. Awareness of that fact, plus the fact that the Steelers are in some kind of a half-reset (new coaching staff, same Aaron Rodgers at quarterback), spells Cincinnati finding a way to win in the Steel City. Pick: Bengals 24, Steelers 20.

Conway: This will be a home game the Bengals are likely favored in by a lot. But this seems like the typical game the Bengals will be expected to win but could end up being one they let slip through their hands. Jacksonville was a surprise team last year, winning 13 games under Liam Coen in his first season as head coach. He's a good coach who understands how to get Trevor Lawrence playing at a high level. Pick: Jaguars 31, Bengals 24

Williams: Jacksonville is coming off a surprising 2025 season in which the Jaguars won the AFC South. They'll be looking to take the next step this season. Last team with the ball wins this entertaining, high-scoring game. The Bengals' rebuilt defense gets a big stop late. Pick: Bengals 35, Jaguars 31

Brennan: The Jaguars have vivid memories of knocking Burrow out of the game at Paycor Stadium last year, but somehow still losing to a team quarterbacked by Jake Browning. Jacksonville will have that disappointment on their minds as they come back to Paycor and take care of their unfinished business. Pick: Jaguars 31, Bengals 28.

Conway: Miami doesn't have a quarterback who can go toe-to-toe with Burrow. This needs to be a game the Bengals dominate and I expect them to do so. Pick: Bengals 34, Dolphins 17

Williams: The Dolphins are expected to be one of the worst teams in the NFL. Look for the Bengals to do what they did in Miami late last season – move the ball at will. Pick: Bengals 42, Dolphins 13

Brennan: The Dolphins stink. This won't be pretty for Miami. Pick: Bengals 41, Dolphins 17.

Conway: Road games in the division are always a challenge. Baltimore has a brand-new coaching staff this season and by this point, I expect their offense to be functioning at a higher level. I have the Bengals and Ravens splitting the series, with each team winning the game at their respective home stadium. Pick: Ravens 24, Bengals 10

Williams: Too bad this isn't in primetime. Former Bengals edge rusher Trey Hendrickson will face his old team for the first time since signing with Baltimore. It'll also be new Ravens coach Jesse Minter's first game in the AFC North rivalry. But this game belongs to Burrow, who'll lead his team to victory in Baltimore for the second straight year. Pick: Bengals 28, Ravens 24

Brennan: This is going to be the toughest divisional game of 2026 for Cincinnati, and the Bengals will have extra preparation for it via the bye week. Perfect timing for Cincinnati because this is a head-to-head between the AFC North's two frontrunners. Pick: Bengals 27, Ravens 24.

Conway: This game will be closer than it probably should, but the Bengals have a far better team than the Titans. Tennessee won't be able to hang on offense, and Cincinnai will win. Pick: Bengals 34, Titans 24

Williams: The Titans are bad. Bengals cruise in this one. Pick: Bengals 35, Titans 17

Brennan: This will be an ugly and unsatisfying victory for Cincinnati. The Bengals will be a week out from their first game on European soil since 2019, and with that comes ticket requests, travel arrangements for family and significant others, and so on. Amidst ample distractions, the Bengals stumble into a victory against an overmatched Titans team. Pick: Bengals 30, Titans 27.

Conway: Burrow has been asking for an international game for a few years now. It's hard to see him not playing his best. The Falcons' quarterback situation is a mess, and regardless of if Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix is starting, it won't be enough. Pick: Bengals 21, Falcons 13

Williams: Burrow on an international stage. He was made for games like this. Pick: Bengals 20, Falcons 14

Brennan: Burrow will look right at home at the Santiago Bernabéu Stadium, the home field of famous Spanish soccer club, Real Madrid. The stadium has served as the home field to some of the greatest soccer players of all time. This will be a classic case of Burrow seizing the moment on a grand stage and manifesting a game to remember (against a bad Falcons team). Pick: Bengals 41, Falcons 10.

Conway: This game has the makings to be one that doesn't fall in the Bengals favor on a short week returning from Madrid, Spain. But I believe the Bengals will sweep the Steelers this season because I don't think much of Pittsburgh's roster this season. Pick: Bengals 17, Steelers 14

Williams: Aaron Rodgers threw four TDs and dinked and dunked the Bengals' defense in last season's primetime game at Paycor Stadium, but the Bengals held on for the rare close victory. Look for the Steelers to avenge the Week 3 loss and get their fifth win in the last six seasons in Cincinnati. Pick: Steelers 23, Bengals 21

Brennan: The NFL schedule-makers don't bake in rest time coming off games abroad like they used to, so get ready to see a sluggish Bengals team. But Cincinnati still finds a way to sweep the season series against Pittsburgh because, just like in their first meeting of the year, Cincinnati knows it can't afford to drop this one if they're going to achieve their lofty goals. Pick: Bengals 20, Steelers 17.

Conway: This is the game where I think the travel from an international game and a primetime game gets to the Bengals. Two years ago, the Bengals were supposed to dominate the Commanders on "Monday Night Football" and got blown out. When healthy, Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels has been a problem. Pick: Commanders 27, Bengals 21

Williams: Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels is coming off a rough 2025 season. But remember, he burst onto the NFL scene with a breakout, primetime performance at Paycor Stadium in 2024. He'll follow that script to end. Pick: Commanders 30, Bengals 27

Brennan: You've got to be reasonable about this game, which the Bengals will lose. Cincinnati will be coming off hosting a division rival on Sunday Night Football and playing in Madrid a week prior to that. There's no way the Bengals go 3-0 in that stretch, but they'll still look competitive while running on fumes against the Commanders. Nothing to panic about here. The Bengals are only human. Pick: Commanders 31, Bengals 21.

Conway: The Bengals are a better team than the Saints. This will be a win for the Bengals. Pick: Bengals 45, Saints 21

Williams: Good time for a warmup game for a December playoff push. Pick: Bengals 42, Saints 20

Brennan: Even a tired Bengals team with a short week of preparation is good enough to trounce the Saints. Pick: Bengals 40, Saints 10.

Conway: It's hard to predict who will be the starting quarterback for Cleveland, and it won't matter. The Bengals won't have Myles Garrett to deal with for the first time in the Burrow era. It won't be pretty as it never is in Cleveland, but Cincinnati wins. Pick: Bengals 21, Browns 13

Williams: Zac Taylor's teams play like dog doo-doo in the Dawg Pound. The Bengals were lucky to win in Cleveland last season, but the Browns won't be in such a giving mood. Pick: Browns 20, Bengals 13

Brennan: The Bengals don't play well on the shores of Lake Erie, but they're too far along in their mission to return to the postseason at this point to be too bothered by the Browns. Pick: Bengals 28, Browns 17.

Conway: This has the makings to be the game of the year in the AFC. I fully expect the Bengals and Chiefs to be in competition for the AFC's top seed at this point in the season. Ultimately, I think veteran head coach Andy Reid and defensive coordinator Steve Spagnulo will have a game plan that will create challenges for the Bengals. Pick: Chiefs 31, Bengals 28

Williams: It won't be like those Bengals-Chiefs battles of a few years ago, when these were the elite teams in the AFC. But hey, it's still the Chiefs. Burrow vs. Patrick Mahomes. National TV. Playoff hunt. Paycor will be rockin'. Pick: Bengals 24, Chiefs 23

Brennan: A late-season, late-afternoon primetime game against the Chiefs? Paycor Stadium will be the hottest ticket in America. Burrow makes it an evening for Cincinnati to savor. Pick: Bengals 29, Chiefs 28.

Conway: The Panthers were a team that got hot at the end of the 2025 season, but I don't see it continuing in 2026. Bengals are rolling at this point in the season. Pick: Bengals 38, Panthers 14

Williams: Burrow is 2-0 in his career against Carolina, both double-digit victories. No way he'll lose this one in a playoff push. Pick: Bengals 35, Panthers 20

Brennan: On the road in Charlotte following an exhilarating win against the Chiefs smells like a potential letdown. Pick: Panthers 29, Bengals 24.

Conway: I expect the Colts to be a good team this year if quarterback Daniel Jones can stay healthy. Defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo will lean on his experience coaching against Burrow and Co. every day in practice when he served as the Bengals' defensive coordinator for six seasons, and I think Indy will win this game. Pick: Colts 21, Bengals 17

Williams: It will be the first time seeing Colts defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo since he was fired by the Bengals after the 2024 season. He'll draw up the perfect game plan to frustrate Burrow and the Bengals' receivers. Pick: Colts 21, Bengals 17

Brennan: The Lou Anarumo Revenge Game. Pick: Colts 24, Bengals 16.

Conway: This game will be electric at Paycor Stadium. The Bengals will understand the magnitude of this game and will play well in front of a massive crowd. Pick: Bengals 28, Ravens 22

Williams: Finally, the Bengals get a primetime home game against the Ravens after playing at night in Baltimore the last four seasons. Minter will return to Cincinnati, where he played college ball at Mount Saint Joseph University. This is for the AFC North championship. The Ravens will get payback for the early season loss in an overtime thriller, ending the Bengals' playoff hopes. Pick: Ravens 41, Bengals 38

Brennan: The Ravens have playoff-caliber talent and are desperate to gain ground in the postseason race. They solidify their place in the standings by winning at Paycor Stadium. Pick: Ravens 31, Bengals 24.

Conway: Once again, the Bengals will close out their regular season against the Browns. This will be a win, with Cincinnati playing for seeding in the AFC at this point. Pick: Bengals 34, Browns 10

Williams: The Bengals need this one to lock up a playoff spot, and they'll take care of business. Pick: Bengals 24, Browns 14

Brennan: Spark the locker room stogies. This is the proverbial "hat and t-shirt game" for the Bengals because they'll clinch the AFC North with a win. Welcome back to "the tournament." Pick: Bengals 29, Browns 10.

Conway: The Bengals will be the AFC's No. 2 seed and host a playoff game against the Los Angeles Chargers. I have the Bengals advancing to the divisional round and beating the Denver Broncos at Paycor Stadium to advance to the AFC Championship Game in Kansas City where the season will come to an end.

Williams: The Bengals win on the road in the wild-card game, but will lose to Buffalo in the divisional round.

Brennan: The Bengals get on a roll at Paycor Stadium by winning the wild card game and hosting the divisional round, but that's where the run ends as the Broncos trip Cincinnati up in the second round.

title: Polasek's rise through the ranks to Mountain West rookie North Dakota St. was launched by hard labor
description: The effort and energy Tim Polasek has poured into North Dakota State's football program on the climb to the FBS can be easily sourced back to his rural roots.  As a small-college quarterback on summer and winter breaks, and later to supplement a meager income as he launched a career in coaching, Polasek worked grueling jobs as a logger in the woods of central Wisconsin and on the overnight shift at a steel mill near his tiny hometown of Iola.  “I learned a lot there: That could be you if you don't graduate college and pursue something,” said Polasek, who is 28-3 with the Bison since becoming head coach in 2024.
fullText:
FARGO, N.D. (AP) — The effort and energy Tim Polasek has poured into North Dakota State's football program on the climb to the FBS can be easily sourced back to his rural roots.

As a small-college quarterback on summer and winter breaks, and later to supplement a meager income as he launched a career in coaching, Polasek worked grueling jobs as a logger in the woods of central Wisconsin and on the overnight shift at a steel mill near his tiny hometown of Iola.

Appreciation for the unglamourous work as a small-college assistant sure comes quick with that background.

"I learned a lot there: That could be you if you don't graduate college and pursue something," said Polasek, who is 28-3 with the Bison since becoming head coach in 2024. "Seeing those tough jobs and other people having to execute that every day really always makes it an honor and a privilege to be the leader of this program."

Having handily beaten Jacksonville State and Fordham in their first two games, the Bison will face one of their biggest tests as a first-year FBS team on Saturday night: Their Mountain West Conference opener at Air Force.

Though five of the strongest programs — Boise State, Colorado State, Fresno State, San Diego State and Utah State — departed this year to restore the Pac-12, the Mountain West restocked with UTEP and North Dakota State and Northern Illinois as football-only members to join holdovers Air Force, Hawaii, Nevada, New Mexico, San Jose State, UNLV and Wyoming.

There's enough relative proximity to the league's geographic footprint and like-minded public institutions for NDSU to see a long-term home that now offers the chance — albeit an annual long shot — to make the College Football Playoff. The Bison won 10 national championships over two decades in the FCS after collecting eight national titles at lower levels.

"We weren't going to go just to go," athletic director Matt Larsen said. "It really had to be the right fit."

Polasek was offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at Wyoming from 2021-23 under head coach Craig Bohl, his former boss at NDSU. Having spent four seasons as the offensive line coach at Iowa before that, Polasek took the job at Wyoming with an eye toward becoming a head coach himself.

"It was really critical for me to go to Iowa and Wyoming and not be one of the top two or three teams picked in the preseason every year and learn those hard lessons," said Polasek, who turned 47 last month. "There was always chatter that NDSU would fit in the Mountain West."

After becoming the all-time leading passer at Concordia University, an NCAA Division III school near Milwaukee, Polasek spent three years on staff at Wisconsin-Stevens Point. Then he got his first big break with a graduate assistant job under Bohl at North Dakota State, which was two seasons into a jump from Division II to the FCS.

He was put in charge of the running backs a year later, added tight ends to his responsibilities after three more seasons, and returned from a one-year stint at Northern Illinois in 2014 as NDSU's offensive coordinator and running backs coach under head coach Chris Klieman.

Then Polasek got a taste of Big Ten play at Iowa, learning the value of "being brilliant at the basics" under longtime head coach Kirk Ferentz before the jump to Wyoming.

"The second thing I learned from Coach Ferentz is if you treat people right you can cultivate an environment where it's fun to show up to work," Polasek said last month in his office at the Fargodome. "No matter if the portal or NIL and all this stuff exists or not, hey, let's treat each other with respect. Everybody in the building should be able to dance to the music the way they want to dance to it."

The upperclassmen on NDSU's roster were recruited by the previous staff under Matt Entz, who's now the head coach at Fresno State. Polasek's enthusiasm for and experience with the program was immediately palpable to those players.

"He's just hard-nosed and he loves football and he knows the game and he's a people person," said third-year wide receiver and kick returner Jackson Williams. "He's going to take care of us, but at the same time he's going to push us to our limits."

title: Justice Department opens federal investigation into Clippers' dealings with Kawhi Leonard
description: The NBA brought the hammer down on the Clippers, but they may now face even more legal issues.
fullText:
The NBA brought the hammer down on the LA Clippers and owner Steve Ballmer for circumventing the salary cap to funnel more money to Kawhi Leonard — and now federal prosecutors are looking into the matter.

The Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation into the Clippers' efforts to secure "no-show" endorsement deals for Kawhi Leonard, the New York Times reports. This investigation is being run out of the U.S. Attorney's Office in Brooklyn, the office that has traditionally looked into issues with professional sports leagues.

The investigation is in its earliest stages, and it's unclear what, if any, federal charges could come out of it, according to the report.

The Justice Department investigation comes in addition to the Securities and Exchange Commission looking into Daktronics' role in the scandal, as it had an endorsement deal with Leonard despite never having had a celebrity endorser before and there being no evidence Leonard did anything for the company. Daktronics is publicly traded, and the SEC is tasked with protecting shareholders.

The NBA oversaw a year-long investigation of its own into the Clippers working to circumvent the salary cap with Leonard and last month came down with the harshest penalties ever imposed on a team:

• The Clippers surrender five first-round draft picks (2029, 2030, 2031, 2032, and 2033).

• The Clippers are fined $30 million.

• Clippers owner Steve Ballmer is suspended from anything to do with the team or the league for one year.

• Clippers President of Business Operations Gillian Zucker is suspended for one year, while President of Basketball Operations Lawrence Frank is suspended for six months.

• Kawhi Leonard must pay a $700,000 fine, and his already-fired business manager, Dennis Robertson (better known as "Uncle Dennis"), is banned from conducting NBA business for five years.'

Ballmer and the Clippers have steadfastly denied any wrongdoing and released this statement after the NBA released its findings and punishments.

"We vehemently reject the NBA's findings, which are the result of a heavily biased investigation seeking to justify a predetermined narrative rather than facts and evidence. What the league told us privately differs from what it announced today publicly, and they have not held themselves close to the standard Commissioner [Adam] Silver set at the start of this investigation to ensure its fairness and accuracy."

The Clippers attorney also sent a letter to the league, but the franchise's only recourse now is the courts, and legal experts have suggested that is a serious uphill fight for Ballmer and the Clippers.

Now, that might not even be the worst of their legal troubles.

title: Sabalenka storms past Pegula to reach US Open final in bid for three-peat

fullText:
Top seed Aryna Sabalenka stormed past Jessica Pegula in straight sets on Thursday to reach the US Open final for fourth straight year and keep her bid for a rare three-peat on track.

The Belarusian -- who will surrender her world number one ranking to Elena Rybakina even if she earns the title -- was simply unstoppable in a 7-5, 6-2 victory on Arthur Ashe Stadium, where she beat Pegula en route to US Open victories in 2024 and 2025.

Sabalenka, bidding to join Chris Evert and Serena Williams as the only women to win three straight US Open titles, struck 29 winners, including seven aces, pounding third-seeded Pegula remorselessly with her powerful groundstrokes.

She will take on the winner of the later semi-final between second-seeded Rybakina and fourth-seeded Coco Gauff in Saturday's title match.

On the evidence of her semi-final win, Sabalenka will head into the final bristling with confidence after producing her best performance of the tournament to snuff out Pegula's dream of a first ever Grand Slam title.

"I'm super happy I was able to play such tennis," said Sabalenka, who sent down seven aces and 29 winners. "I was so desperate to win. I wanted it so badly."

Both Sabalenka and Gauff served superbly in a tense first set that came down to the final game.

Sabalenka's frustration at her inability to make any headway against Pegula's serve showed with shrugs and a bounced racquet, but she maintained her focus and was rewarded as Pegula, feeling the pressure to stay in the set as she served down 6-5, fell behind 0-40.

The American saved one set point but couldn't salvage the next as Sabalenka seized control of the point with a fierce service return and took the set when Pegula hit a forehand into the net.

Sabalenka kept rolling in the second set, attacking Pegula's suspect second serve and seizing a break for a 3-1 lead when she lasered a forehand into the corner.

She sealed the victory with another break, unleashing another thunderous forehand on match point.

It was more Grand Slam disappointment for Pegula, who fell to Sabalenka in the 2024 final -- her only major final to date -- and in the semi-finals last year.

Sabalenka, 28, has had a slow summer since winning back to back titles at Indian Wells and Miami in March, opening the door to Rybakina to end her reign atop the rankings that began in October 2024.

Rybakina was bracing for a hostile reception against Gauff, who has been a favorite of New York crowds since her US Open debut as a 15-year-old wild card in 2019.

Their head to head record is 1-1, but Gauff's win came back in 2023 with Rybakina taking their most recent encounter in the semi-finals at Toronto just last month.

The Kazakh star has appeared untroubled by the heel injury that clouded her preparations for the Open, leaving her unable to walk without pain for several days.

Rybakina had been closing in on Sabalenka's number one ranking for weeks. Having secured it, she was trying to stay laser focused on the hunt for a third Grand Slam title to go with Australian Open title she captured in January -- four years after she lifted her first major trophy at Wimbledon.

"Mostly you think about the titles in the end of the day," she said.

The men's semi-finals are on Friday, when eighth-seeded Ben Shelton takes on 11th seed Frances Tiafoe in an all-American clash.

Shelton took out defending champion and seven-time Grand Slam winner Carlos Alcaraz in an epic quarter-final that ended at 3:34 am on Wednesday -- the latest finish in tournament history.

"Big Ben" and "Big Foe" will duel for a chance to end American men's 23-year Grand Slam title drought -- stretching back to Andy Roddick's 2003 US Open victory.

The winner will take on either top-seeded Alexander Zverev or unseeded Russian Karen Khachanov -- who ousted third-seeded Felix Auger-Aliassime on the way to his third career Grand Slam semi.

title: Sabalenka powers into fourth successive US Open final
description: Aryna Sabalenka may have lost the world number one spot but she is determined to keep her US Open title. The 28-year-old from Belarus, who will be overtaken by Elena Rybakina at the top of the rankings on Monday, overpowered Jessica Pegula 7-5, 6-2 to reach a fourth successive Flushing Meadows final.
fullText:
Aryna Sabalenka may have lost the world number one spot but she is determined to keep her US Open title.

The 28-year-old from Belarus, who will be overtaken by Elena Rybakina at the top of the rankings on Monday, overpowered Jessica Pegula 7-5, 6-2 to reach a fourth successive Flushing Meadows final.

The two-time defending champion took her winning streak in New York to 19 matches and is now one victory away from the 'three-peat'.

American third seed Pegula, beaten by Sabalenka in the 2024 final, had served superbly during the first set, winning 18 out of 20 points behind her first serve.

That was until 5-6, when Sabalenka suddenly unleashed three blistering returns to bring up three set points, taking the second when Pegula's forehand fell into the net.

More break points arrived in the fourth game of the second set and a 146 km/h return put the top seed in total control.

A business-like victory was wrapped up in an hour and 20 minutes and celebrated with a simple clenched fist.

"No complaints, I'm super happy to be able to play such tennis," she said. "I was so desperate to win, I wanted it badly."

title: Texas baseball: Exhibition, SEC schedules set for Longhorns ahead of 2027 season
description: On Thursday, Texas announced that it will head to Round Rock's Dell Diamond on Oct. 3 for an exhibition game against Houston. The first pitch for the Longhorns and Cougars is set for 12 p.m.
fullText:
The Texas baseball team will play ball this fall.

On Thursday, Texas announced that it will head to Round Rock's Dell Diamond on Oct. 3 for an exhibition game against Houston. The first pitch for the Longhorns and Cougars is set for 12 p.m.

The nine-inning scrimmage will be UT's only fall contest.

Texas holds a 99-35-2 lead in its all-time series with Houston. This past March, the Cougars recorded a 9-7 win at the Longhorns' expense in Houston.

Texas reached the College World Series in 2026 as head coach Jim Schlossnagle finished up his second season with the program. The Longhorns are set to return 14 letterwinners in 2027, and UT is adding both a highly-rated transfer class and a top-five recruiting class to its roster.

Thursday's announcement about the Houston exhibition wasn't the only schedule-related news that was released by Texas this week. On Tuesday, the SEC schedule for UT was also revealed. The Longhorns will host South Carolina (March 25-27), Tennessee (April 9-11), Arkansas (April 23-25), Vanderbilt (April 30-May 2) and Texas A&M (May 14-16) this spring while also visiting LSU (March 19-21), Alabama (April 2-4), Florida (April 16-18), Oklahoma (May 7-9) and Georgia (May 20-22).

title: Five Plays: Ole Miss Fourth Quarter
description: The action continued to ratchet up in the fourth quarter with both teams trading big plays and touchdowns. The defenses both left a lot to be desired, but we did get a glimpse into how Mark Ivey will call a close game going forward. I went a little more rapid-fire with this post to fit […]
fullText:
The action continued to ratchet up in the fourth quarter with both teams trading big plays and touchdowns. The defenses both left a lot to be desired, but we did get a glimpse into how Mark Ivey will call a close game going forward. I went a little more rapid-fire with this post to fit in more plays, so excuse my brevity.

Ole Miss had a bit of a field day against Cover 3 on Sunday, with this being the second touchdown of the day against the coverage. The corners and the deep safety are responsible for a third of the field, and with all coverages like this, you are responsible for the deepest man in your area. Sometimes, you just get beat, and this is essentially what happened here.

Trinidad Chambliss initially looks right on this play. He's looking at a quick hitch route, but I don't think he had any intention of throwing the ball. He takes a quick two-step drop and stares down the receiver to that side. He then takes a hop back to reset his feet as he whips his head back to the left and launches a perfectly floated ball in between the corner and safety. This is just elite quarterback play.

Jabari Mack could do better on this play. He has an underneath defender on this play, so he should be tracking the slot down the field. Instead, he stops his feet with the outside comeback route and isn't in position to make a play on the ball or at least get the receiver down after the catch.

Lance Robinson needs to be better here. He's in a one-on-one matchup on the left side facing a straightforward pass rush from Kam Franklin. Robinson gets good depth with his kick steps, but he opens his hips and chest too much, which allows Franklin to toss him to his left. Robinson should be moving back to center once Anwar O'neal is healthy, but that could be a few weeks from now.

A potential change we will likely see with Mark Ivey calling the plays on defense is an uptick in aggression. On this play, he mugs up the line with 8 guys, and he actually brings 7. Chambliss looks to go to the double move on the outside, but the blitz gets the job done by gettin gon him so quickly that he has to scramble.

I loved seeing this on second and long, especially with the Cards being beaten for long touchdowns in the third quarter. A lot of coaches talk about making mistakes at full speed. It's a way of saying always play your hardest, and we'll deal with the mistakes. I've also always taken it to mean always play with aggression. There are times when coaches should make calls with the same mentality they want their players to have.

I wanted to clip this third down call because I felt it really showed how dynamic this offense can be. There are four threats on this play for a defense to deal with. You have jet motion to Tre Richardson after he already scored a touchdown on a jet sweep. You have Lincoln Kienholz, who has already broken a big run on a play with jet sweep action. You have Keyjuan Brown, who is an obvious threat to get a yard with a tough run. Then you have Jaleel Skinner, who can just run a quick route for an easy first down.

It's just a basic third-and-short pickup, but I really do think it highlights the level of versatility that Jeff Brohm has to work with this season.

It's pretty nice to have a quarterback who can just mug a future NFL draft pick into the ground like this.

I said it before the season started, and I'll repeat it here. Lawayne McCoy has real potential to be a star. The catch on this play is impressive enough as he keeps his feet in bounds. But to make the first defender miss by running the wrong direction, then following that up with a stiff arm that is essentially behind his back, is pretty unbelievable.

Linc also does a good job again climbing the pocket when he feels pressure. He keeps his eyes up and down the field, looking for someone to come open before delivering a very nice ball to the sideline. This was another great sign of his potential down the road.

I really liked this play by TJ Banks at the bottom of the line here. He walks up late to put himself in position to set the edge to the strong side of the formation. When Ole Miss goes to the other side, he tracks the play down the line and sells out to get to the running back's legs, which ends the play. Over the course of a game, plays like this matter so much more than realized.

Banks' play leads to third and medium, and Ivey brings pressure again. This time he mugs up the line with tight Cover 0 behind it. This was a solid gamble with the Cards down a touchdown, and Ole Miss being a big play away from ending the game.

Ivey brings overloaded pressure from Chambliss' right again, and it works because Antonio Watts gets wide and takes away the first option in the process. Chambliss has to wait, and by the time he has a clear view again, the play is dead, and he has to throw it away. As much as we all want to see pressures get home, it can work just as well if you can just force an incompletion.

Remember in the second quarter when Linc got out of the pocket and completely missed his receiver breaking down the field as he scrambled? This was much better. He gets a six-man pressure, so he immediately looks to get moving out of the pocket to avoid the rush and extend the play. He and Isaac Brown look like they're sharing a brain on this play because Brown senses the hesitation from Linc and looks to break up the field. Linc gives a quick pump fake to draw the defender and drops a nice throw in stride to Brown.

We got the full Lincoln Kienholz experience on Sunday, and it was capped off with this run. He gets the space he needs with the motion from the back before he does an outstanding job of "pressing" the hole. He gets up the field, which forces the defense to constrict towards him. You can see #3 for Ole Miss give up his contain to get inside in hopes of catching Linc at the second level. Linc then breaks outside towards the pylon for the big touchdown.

There are running backs who can't get this down.

I won't kill Antonio Watts for not being in a position to make this play, but he's so close to making this play if he didn't take an extra step to the outside. Watts is responsible for the flat on this play, so when the running back leaks out of the backfield, Watts starts to widen out with him. I just can't help but think that if Watts takes one hop to his left instead of three, he could have picked this pass off.

I'll start by saying that I don't think anyone could have stopped this completion, but Kaleb Beasley maybe could have had the best chance. This is Cover 3 again for the Cards, and Ole Miss looks to beat it again with a player running through the defense into a seam. Deuce Alexander scored earlier in the game on a similar route, but in this situation, there is not a deep threat to account for.

This is where Beasley possibly could have made a play. He is responsible for the deep middle of the field, but with no threats, he could have stepped up to try to take away this throw. You can see that he has what I call "bad eyes". He's looking to his right to see what the outside receiver is doing, when he isn't responsible for that receiver. At worst, that receiver could run a deep post and get behind him, but with the formation, the corner would follow because there is no one else in his zone.

I don't want this to come off as me killing any of these defenders. I just see the opportunities for some plays to be made. Chambliss is an elite quarterback. He's going to beat you more times than not.

title: How Should the Cubs Rotation Be Managed Down the Stretch of 2026?
description: In 2026, the Cubs' starters have been a major storyline. While the bullpen's struggle is the biggest issue, the rotation has been concerning. fullText:
In 2026, the Cubs' starters have been a major storyline. While the bullpen's struggle is the biggest issue, the rotation has been concerning. The pitching struggles have severely impacted the team in the second half of the season. When looking at the playoff picture, their lead has diminished, and both San Diego and Arizona are within three games of Chicago. However, there is hope for the Cubs starters.

Chicago has had a very up-and-down year from their starters. Injuries have plagued the team, as nearly all pitchers miss time. A busy trade deadline had things looking promising. While a few have had good starts, the team has struggled to find consistency. That said, the Cubs' starter hierarchy has clearly shifted. If Chicago wishes to make a run in the playoffs, relying on the top three Cubs starters needs to be the move.

Clay Holmes has been the top Cubs starter since he joined the team. With Chicago, he is 2-3 with a 3.51 ERA. The ERA is inflated by his last start, in which he allowed eight runs in 4.1 innings. Without that game, he was showing his ace potential. Down the stretch of the season, Holmes will need to show his talent and give the Cubs valuable length.

The other newcomer, Kevin Gausman, has also been solid since joining Chicago. His most recent start against the Brewers was rough, allowing six earned runs. He has had mixed results in his seven starts, with a 5.31 ERA. However, he is giving good length, going six or seven innings in most starts. Additionally, his valuable playoff experience makes him a key piece of the Cubs rotation.

Of the three starters, Matthew Boyd is the only one who has been with them all year. Boyd has struggled with injuries and inconsistency, but still has given valuable innings. Like Gausman, he can go fairly deep into games. He is 8-4 with a 4.03 ERA in 109.1 innings. His experience with Chicago could see him start one of the first two games come playoff time.

The Cubs starters get harder to predict following those three. Shota Imanaga is the only pitcher who has stayed healthy, going 156.1 innings. At times, he has been in great control of his stuff. However, he has also allowed 33 home runs, tied for most in the league. That was a concern after last year, and it has become the major factor that makes it hard to trust him in important games.

Following Imanaga, David Peterson had been serving as the fifth starter. Similar to the other Cubs starters, he has had a very up-and-down season. Since the Cubs traded for him, he has a 4.41 ERA and a 4-2 record in 63.1 innings. The lefty has used groundballs effectively, and with the Cubs' defense, he looks like a different version of himself. Even if he does not start in the playoffs, he is a quality pitcher who is sure to be in the Cubs' pitching plans.

In terms of playing multiple roles, no one is better than Javier Assad. Assad has spent time in Iowa until his most recent call-up. On September 5th, he made a start against the Marlins, where he went 4.2 innings, allowing three runs and five walks. It remains to be seen what they will do with him, but using a sixth starter could be wise. Assad staying in the rotation would allow the other starters to get an extra day of rest, while the bullpen could stay fresher.

Now, with all six candidates listed, the Cubs could go a few different ways. They could stick with their current five. To win in the playoffs, you need good pitching. If you stick with your current guys, there is hope to get them set before the playoffs. However, that has not worked, as the pitching setbacks may be costing them a playoff spot.

With that in mind, moving Assad into the rotation, either as a sixth starter or replacing one of the other ones, could be the move. The Cubs starters need to set the tone. The bullpen can not hold a lead right now, so starters need to go longer. Making a change ensures that the best players are pitching as much. Assas has always been a solid piece, and right now Chicago can not be picky.

Chicago has fallen in the playoff standings, and pitching is the major reason why. If they wish to hold onto their playoff spot, the Cubs starters need to take control of games. It has been a weird season, and a devastating last few weeks, but they can not give up. Their bats are strong, and the defense is one of the best in the league. If the starting rotation can hold games steady enough, then they may be able to make a postseason run.

title: Red Sox Spent Last Week Getting House in 'Order' Regarding Injuries
description: The Red Sox are making a very wise decision by doing so.
fullText:
Red Sox Spent Last Week Getting House in 'Order' Regarding Injuries originally appeared on NESN. 

The Boston Red Sox have given themselves a good chance to not only win a World Series, but also take things easy over the next couple of weeks.

The last thing the Red Sox want to do is deal with any more injuries than they already have, and at 80-67, they're likely not to win the American League East. With a six-game lead in the American League Wild Card race, there truly isn't a whole lot to worry about.

While we've seen some crazy things happen throughout the campaign, and the Red Sox can't guarantee that they're in the playoffs until things finish, they have to feel pretty good about where things stand.

According to the latest from their MLB.com writer, the Red Sox are spending the last couple of weeks of the regular season, and have already done so, by being smart and getting guys healthy.

"I think that's a pretty good read. There has been a bit of a sea change since the lost series in New York at the end of August minimized the chances of the Sox getting home field for a Wild Card Series.

title: Abington football runs Longmeadow off the field in season-opening win
description: A key stop by the Green Wave defense and a potent rushing attack were the difference for Abington on opening night.
fullText:
ABINGTON -- Success came and went for Abington high school football in its 2026 season opener. But enough Green Waves were made to outlast its opponent.

After trading haymakers all night, Abington, a Division 6 program, delivered the final blow to Div. 4 Longmeadow 43-21 in the first game of the season at home on Frolio Memorial Field on Thursday, Sept. 10.

For most of the game the Green Wave outlasted a relentless Lancer team with its bruising and dynamic run game and an opportunistic special teams unit. But it was a defensive stand that sealed Abington's victory.

With 9:20 to play, trailing 35-21, Longmeadow had a fourth-and-goal from Abington's 1-yard line. The Lancers handed it off to 6-foot, 207-pound running back Maury Garrett lll, but he was stonewalled and driven back nearly eight yards for a turnover on downs.

The play kept Longmeadow from bringing it back to a one-score game. Abington's offense capitalized and finished a 91-yard touchdown drive with a 15-yard run by sophomore Jake Lehman for the game's final score with 5:29 remaining.

Abington's offense totaled 260 rushing yards on the evening. Five of the six touchdowns came via the ground game. Lehman had the highest rush total on the night, accounting for 84 of those yards and a pair of touchdowns. He scored Abington's first points of the season in the first quarter on a 24-yard scamper after Longmeadow scored on its first possession to go up 7-0.

Junior Daniel Pifer led the team in total offensive yards with 103 (68 rushing, 35 receiving) and two touchdowns. Senior Nazir Paulding tallied 57 rushing yards and had a 55-yard punt return touchdown for a total of 112 all-purpose yards and two total touchdowns.

Abington's offense didn't punt until the final drive of the game.

title: Gonzaga’s 2027 Recruiting Class Could Be Special: The Latest Rankings Update
description: Updated rankings push 2027 commit Dooney Johnson towards the Top 10 as Jalen Davis and Gene Roebuck remain key targets.
fullText:
It is never too early to start planning for next season, even if Gonzaga's current eligibility situation and roster uncertainty heading into the 2026-27 season make planning feel borderline irresponsible. The Bulldogs' entire offseason has been consumed by NCAA uncertainty thanks to waiver cases, court orders, and a nightmarishly litigious governing body seemingly hell-bent on ruining the sport to make a point about… fairness? I guess?

Hopefully, once this summer's NCAA litigation mess is settled, Gonzaga and 360+ other teams in D1 college basketball will have actual parameters for who is eligible, when they are eligible, and why. For now, though, the clearest way to view Gonzaga's 2027-28 roster is through its likely departures and the 2027 commits that could be asked to fill the vacant roster spots.

Nothing is totally certain in college basketball anymore, but it's more than likely that after this coming season, Xaivian Lee, Javon Bennett, Chauncey Wiggins, Nathan De Sousa, and Braden Huff have exhausted all of their remaining competitive eligibility (that is, of course, assuming Lee, De Sousa, Bennett, and Wiggins actually gain and maintain it in the first place). Perhaps equally consequential is whether Davis Fogle and/or Massamba Diop develop into the 2027 NBA Draft departures many are speculating they will, and whether Izan Almansa receives clearance and remains in college, and, because this is now college basketball, how many other eligible players decide the transfer portal offers a better path.

The good news is that Gonzaga already has a legitimate foundation for 2027, and that foundation has looked better with every evaluation period. 2027 commit Dooney Johnson is a lock for the Zags, but he is not the only high-end piece the Zags are pursuing. If Gonzaga can add either Jalen Davis or Gene Roebuck, or, in the ideal scenario, both, the Bulldogs' 2027-28 freshman class could quickly become one of the most exciting in the country.

Dooney Johnson committed to the Bulldogs in October 2025, one of the earliest commitments in the cycle, when he was already a coveted four-star prospect from Milwaukee Juneau in Wisconsin. Most importantly, the Zags locked him down before a full summer on the Nike EYBL circuit pushed him into a different tier of the class. Johnson is now No. 11 in Rivals' post-summer 2027 rankings, after sitting No. 31 in Rivals' May update and No. 12 entering July. He is the highest-ranked player currently committed in the 2027 class.

Playing for Team Herro, Johnson led the program in scoring at 14.9 points per game over 22 EYBL contests, despite ranking only fifth on the team in minutes at 23.6 per game. He added 4.4 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game, finishing second in assists and third in rebounds. In EYBL league play, Rivals recorded him at 14.3 points, 4.1 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 1.7 steals per game. Team Herro reached the Peach Jam semifinals, where Johnson put up 16 points, four rebounds, and three assists against the Florida Rebels. He went 6-for-11 on two-point attempts in that game, a useful snapshot of the part of his game that has driven his rise: getting downhill and living in the paint.

Gonzaga bound Dooney Johnson is a future pro! @thedooneywatch @NikeEYB pic.twitter.com/j7mSbedrNS

Johnson earned Nike EYBL First Team recognition alongside Rivals prospects ranked No. 2 DeMarcus Henry, No. 4 Beckham Black, No. 8 Cayden Daughtry and No. 10 Lewis Uvwo. He also stood out at the Pangos All-America Camp and the NBPA Top 100, meaning his ranking rise was not built on a single Peach Jam weekend. It reflected a summer in which he continued to show up against the best competition available to his class.

At 6-foot-7, Johnson has the dimensions of a wing but plays like a lead guard. He uses his length and physicality to barrel into traffic, can make the next pass once defenses collapse, and has the size to see passing lanes and bother opposing ball handlers on the other end. Johnson has the tools to become the kind of large, disruptive perimeter defender Gonzaga has increasingly valued in addition to being the kind of highly physical, high-IQ floor general the Zags had in Jalen Suggs.

The long-term swing skill is the jumper. Johnson made 26.6% of his EYBL threes on a substantial 5.0 attempts per game, so it would be dishonest to treat outside shooting as a settled strength. But there is a difference between an unproven shooter who avoids attempting threes and a high-usage creator willing to take them while carrying a major offensive burden. Johnson still has one more season in high school (which he will spend in Florida after transferring to East River High School in Orlando for his senior year) to focus on that part of his game. The more difficult traits to teach – his positional size, force, passing feel, defensive activity, and comfort operating with the ball – are already in the bag.

Whatever uncertainty surrounds Gonzaga's 2027-28 roster, Johnson increasingly looks like the type of prospect around whom a coherent one can be built.

If Dooney Johnson is the oversized initiator Gonzaga can build around, Jalen Davis may be the cleanest possible backcourt complement. The 6-foot-3 Bremerton product has emerged from the summer as the top-ranked player in Washington and one of the country's premier 2027 guards. Davis is No. 18 nationally in Rivals' most recent 2027 rankings, one spot ahead of fellow Washington standout Christian Gurdak, and is the state's highest-ranked prospect on the list. Gonzaga offered Davis in July 2025, made his final 10 and will host him for an official visit on Nov. 7.

NEWS: 2027 Top-20 overall recruit Jalen Davis is down to 10 schools, he tells @Rivals.

The 6-3 guard has scheduled five official visits: https://t.co/4TBeDGJjLY pic.twitter.com/nclj1DFlV4

Playing with Thomas' Grind on the Adidas 3SSB circuit, Davis led all 17U scorers at 23.9 points per game while shooting nearly 50% from the field. At Section 7 in June, he scored 39 points in front of Gonzaga coaches during a high-profile matchup with fellow five-star Adan Diggs. As a junior at Bremerton, Davis averaged a staggering 31.5 points, 9.6 rebounds, 5.8 steals, and 5.2 assists per game. He shot 63.9% from the field and 40% from three while leading the Knights to a 26-2 record and a second consecutive Class 2A state championship.

Davis is a powerful scorer who can work out of ball screens, hit jumpers off the catch or dribble, and get to the rim with either hand. His speed and vision mean he can also create for teammates, making him more than a volume scorer. Johnson's size would allow Gonzaga to use Davis in a variety of ways, including as a primary ball handler or an off-ball scorer attacking the openings Johnson creates. Davis would bring the more conventional guard skills that allow an offense to move cleanly from one action to the next: pace, shooting gravity, shot creation, and quick decisions. In short, the Zags would once again have a clean return to the dual playmaking backcourt set that's defined some of its best teams in recent years.

Davis also makes tremendous basketball sense alongside Dooney Johnson. A future backcourt with both players would give Gonzaga two creators with contrasting physical profiles and overlapping offensive versatility, rather than two players competing for identical responsibilities.

Gene Roebuck is not officially committed yet, but word on the street is that he is looking more and more like a Zag by the day. The 6-foot-5 La Mirada, California, wing has also visited UCLA, USC and Cal and still has other trips to make. Still, the momentum appears favorable for Gonzaga. Roebuck has praised Mark Few, said he wanted to return to Spokane, and Gonzaga coaches made a point of seeing him repeatedly during the Adidas 3SSB summer.

Roebuck averaged 19.4 points, 5.6 rebounds, and two assists over 17 Adidas 3SSB games for Dream Vision, making 2.2 threes per game. In his official 3SSB statistical sample, he shot 52% from the field and 42% from three. He then averaged 23 points and five rebounds at the Palmetto Road Championship, including a 36-point performance against Indiana Elite. In Rivals' updated rankings, Roebuck comes in at No. 44 while 247 Sports places him in the top-50 also.

The talented 6-foot-5 guard has a few more visits still in the works 👀 https://t.co/x0eyY2Hdhs pic.twitter.com/2fmEUDtuDN

While Dooney Johnson is a large creator who wants to get downhill and bend defenses, Roebuck is a strong scoring wing who can space the floor, rebound, create a shot when a possession breaks down, and take advantage from the perimeter when defenders collapse inside. If Gonzaga does land him, the excitement should come from the fit itself as much as the hype around his individual player profile.

In an era when college basketball rosters can be remade in a single offseason, there is unusual value in bringing in a freshman class that already fits together. Transfers can fill a hole, and a veteran can change a season, but neither necessarily gives a program the continuity of three players arriving at the same time, learning the system together and developing a shared understanding over multiple years.

That is the real appeal here. Gonzaga's 2027-28 roster remains impossible to predict with total confidence because the NCAA's eligibility process, NBA decisions, and the transfer portal will determine so much of it. But a Johnson-Davis-Roebuck class would give Mark Few something unusually stable amid all that chaos: a group of talented perimeter players who could grow together and provide a foundation long after the rest of the roster picture changes.

Gonzaga has a long way to go before that becomes reality. But with Johnson already committed and Davis and Roebuck firmly on the radar, it is not hard to see why this recruiting class is worth following now, if only as a reaffirming distraction from the hellscape of litigatory upheaval that's defined this year's offseason.

title: Jacoby Brissett appears in interesting trade rumor
description: Could the Cardinals move their starting quarterback if they struggle?
fullText:
The Arizona Cardinals have done a lot to ensure that Jacoby Brissett is their starting quarterback. They made it know that he would be the starter. They gave him about a $10 million raise because he is their starter. He was named a team captain.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler says it could happen.

Arizona's quarterback situation is underplayed, possibly because of the Cardinals' perceived noncontender status and Carson Beck being a third-round pick. But they absolutely have enough talent to move the ball, and Brissett averaged 280.5 passing yards per start over 12 games last season. If Brissett plays well but the Cardinals struggle to win, he could be a trade candidate at midseason. That opens a path for Arizona to see what it has in Beck, who acquitted himself well in the preseason, before considering their 2027 draft options.

It is an interesting possibility. With the Cardinals expected to struggle in 2026, the presumption is that Beck will end up starting before the end of the season. How will Brissett take that, assuming he produces despite winning?

How would the locker room respond to a team captain being traded?

It would totally make sense. Brissett is not the future. He isn't expected to be on the team in 2027, at least right now. It would make sense to try and get something for him if the opportunity were to arise.

This is, though, creating an interesting hypothetical. If the Cardinals are bad, will Brissett be good, or will he return to the level he has played for most of his career, which is pretty ordinary?

It isn't something to worry about yet, but it is something to keep in the back of our minds.

title: A chaotic Warriors season unlocked De'Anthony Melton's game. Now he's ‘full go'
description: Golden State Warriors guard De'Anthony Melton adjusted to an expanded offensive role in 2025-26. He might have to get comfortable with more self-creation duties on a banged-up roster this fall.
fullText:
In a season of dysfunction, De'Anthony Melton, at least, found something that clicked. For a decade, he had packed up pieces of his game and stuffed them away, collecting dust in an NBA attic. He was a point-of-attack defender, and a combo ballhandler, and an opportunistic off-ball shooter. Until 2025-26.

Jimmy Butler tore his ACL, and so did Moses Moody, and Stephen Curry had his own ailing knee. Someone needed to handle the basketball. And so Melton - still working back from his own torn ACL in 2024-25 - brushed off an old bag that hadn't quite seen a spotlight since starring days at Crespi Carmelite High in Los Angeles's San Fernando Valley.

Sometimes it didn't work. Sometimes it did. One thing really did, a little same-hand crossover that often froze bigger defenders. He shook Brooklyn's Nic Claxton in December, and snaked Charlotte's Grant Williams in January, and slithered past Utah's Brice Sensabaugh in March.

"I was f-ing people up with my in-and-out (cross) for some reason," Melton told the Chronicle Thursday, grinning. "I was f-ing people up with my in-and-out. I don't even know why. People was just going for it."

Melton knows this. Get ready for more in-and-out crosses, unless opposing bigs have studied their tape. He'll adapt, if so. He prides himself on that.

"That's something I want to do," Melton said Thursday, asked if he was preparing to shoulder a heavier workload with Golden State's prevailing injuries. "And you should want more of a burden on you, on your shoulders. You know what I mean? That's how valuable you are. And it's like, you're capable of it, so go do it."

Is he capable? Inconclusive. Over 49 games in 2025-26, Melton averaged a career-high 12.3 points per game but wasn't particularly efficient.

He wore many hats last year, and many took time to break in. First came his season debut in December after a year-plus-long recovery from 2024's torn ACL, and a month of visible shooting rust. Then came a budding role as an off-the-bench sparkplug in January. Then came starting off-guard duties in February with Butler and Curry sidelined. Then came a whole heap of self-creation duties in March, alongside a stretch in which Melton yo-yoed between starting and coming off the bench for seven straight games.

"It was weird," Melton said. "It was definitely weird … we had like, damn near three different rosters in one year, you know what I mean? So my role, especially with me, I'm so adaptive and I could do so many different things that my role, it kinda just kept changing."

When the shuffling stopped, the scope of his responsibilities was vast, and unusual. Here are some players who finished second on their respective teams in usage rate (with at least 40 games played) last year: New York All-Star Karl-Anthony Towns, Denver All-Star Jamal Murray, Houston All-Star Alperen Sengun.

"It was just tough," Melton said. "Trying to figure out what we needed as a team, and then what services me best as a player, but then also having to do certain things that - I exerted a lot of energy just trying to create the offense and create advantages and stuff like that.

"And, also, having to go on the other end and guard the best players."

All of this, of course, was slightly complicated by his own season-long ramp-up, as Melton faced a minutes restriction for much of the season and played 30 minutes just twice. The Warriors have to already (ahem) manage Butler and Moody's rehabilitation, manage Curry's knee, manage Kristaps Porzingis' health, and manage the workloads for 36-year-old Draymond Green and 40-year-old Al Horford; they can ill-afford to have another key rotational piece with limited availability this fall.

That, though, was a specific point of conversation in free-agent negotiations this offseason with Golden State. Melton told the Chronicle Thursday that he'll be "full-go" with no restriction in 2026-27, and confirmed he plans to play in back-to-backs, a sorely needed development for the Warriors' roster.

The same self-creation duties may not fall on Melton again - and shouldn't - if Curry misses time. Golden State signed Brandon Williams, Melton's old high school teammate at Crespi, as a potential backup ballhandler. Rising fourth-year guard Brandin Podziemski also took an offensive step in last season's last two months.

But Melton, still, won't be shelving the toolkit.

"It was definitely different," Melton said, reflecting on last year's role. "But, I mean, it also showed me that I could do it. And it's just about doing it consistently."

There's more to San Francisco with the Chronicle.

Álex Rins is done with motorcycle racing. On the eve of the San Marino Grand Prix, the Monster Energy Yamaha rider confirmed he will leave MotoGP at the end of 2026, but ruled out a rumored move to the World Superbike Championship. Instead, Rins will step away from two-wheeled competition entirely and pursue a project on four wheels instead.

The rumors had been building at Magny-Cours, and Rins cleared them up himself during Thursday's media scrum at Misano. Discussions with Go Eleven reportedly fell through, and rather than chase a Plan B in WSBK racing, the 30-year-old Spaniard went a different direction entirely.

"I will not go to Superbike next year," Rins said. "I had two possibilities there. I really want to say thanks to them because they were quite interested in me. But I found another thing that really motivates me more." He added that he can't reveal the new project yet because negotiations are still on-going but hinted that it would be on four wheels instead of two.

"I'm really happy. For sure it was difficult to choose, because all my life in MotoGP, in this championship, many fights, many races, many wins," says Rins. "14 years, more or less. So yeah, I will stop with two wheels."

Rins didn't slam the door completely on bikes. He floated the idea of a limited return in the vein of Cal Crutchlow.

The decision closes a Grand Prix run that began in Moto3 in 2012. Rins finished runner-up in both Moto3 and Moto2 before moving to the premier class with Suzuki in 2017, where he earned five MotoGP wins and 18 podiums. A move to LCR Honda in 2023 delivered a victory in his third race at the Americas GP before a serious Mugello leg injury wrecked his season. His three years with Yamaha have coincided with the M1's decline; he currently sits 20th in the 2026 championship standings.

With Rins out and Fabio Quartararo bound for Honda, Yamaha will line up Jorge Martín and Ai Ogura in 2027.

The Los Angeles Rams, the heavy Super Bowl favorites entering the season, opened the year in the NFL's first-ever game in Melbourne, Australia, against the San Francisco 49ers. The majority of the attention the Rams have gotten this offseason has been centered on the defensive line, which was bolstered by the acquisition of the NFL's single-season sack record holder Myles Garrett and the return of Aaron Donald from retirement.

However, Los Angeles also has one of the most potent offenses in the league, with reigning league MVP Matthew Stafford passing to two of the best wide receivers in the league, Davante Adams and Puka Nacua. Unfortunately for Nacua, he's been caught up in some off-the-field trouble recently.

Ahead of kickoff on Thursday, Nacua sat down with Netflix's Elle Duncan and spoke candidly about his struggles wth alcohol.

"I think I learned that I'm very avoidant of conflict, which is very interesting due to the football nature of… I would like to say I play very physical, just avoidant of the things that I know were causing me stress," Nacua told Duncan.

"Just, I think some of the change in lifestyle that came up to me, becoming a public figure, the stress of performing at a high level," he responded after being asked what was causing him stress. "And then I recently became a father. My son is 10 months old. And navigating that co-parenting relationship with his mother, I would kind of isolate myself to feel like the weight of all the issues and things that I have was stuck on my shoulders, and not being willing to ask for help. I was never one to share my fears and my worries. I was always Finding different ways to escape, I guess, from that tension or that stress."

Puka Nacua opened up about turning to alcohol to cope with the pressures of stardom.

“I was always finding different ways to escape… alcohol was definitely a thing for me.”

Now, the #Rams WR says he wants to become someone his son can be proud of.

(via @NetflixSports) pic.twitter.com/VToMvRw7Ra

— Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) September 10, 2026

"I think one, alcohol was definitely a thing for me," he added about how he looked to escape, "just kind of drowning myself so that the issues and the stress that I was feeling never had the opportunity to be addressed. But right when I entered the rehabilitation center, I was able to have open and honest conversations."

"As it sits right now, at 25 years old, with your whole life in front of you, what are you most looking forward to about who you're becoming?" Duncan asked.

"I'm looking forward most to, um, becoming a person that I think my son will be proud of."

Nacua led the NFL in first downs a season ago with 80 of them. If he can stay focused and out of trouble, there's nothing stopping him from having an offensive player of the year caliber campaign this season.
